title: Two Sum
summary: Find the indices of two numbers that add up to a target.
statement:
Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices `[i, j]` of the two
numbers that add up to `target`, with `i < j`.

Exactly one valid pair exists. You may not use the same element twice, but the array can contain
duplicate values (for example `nums = [3, 3]`, `target = 6`).

A brute-force double loop works. Can you do it in a single pass?

examples.explanation: Duplicates are allowed as long as they are different elements.

hints: For each number, you already know exactly which other value you'd need. How could you check whether you've seen it, quickly?
A HashMap from value to index gives O(1) lookups. As you scan, look up `target - nums[i]` before storing `nums[i]` itself.

seen = empty map of value -> index
for i from 0 to n-1:
    need = target - nums[i]
    if need in seen: return [seen[need], i]
    seen[nums[i]] = i
throw (unreachable: an answer is guaranteed)

The nested-loop approach checks every pair: O(n^2). Storing each value's index in a HashMap turns 'have I seen the complement?' into an O(1) average lookup, so one pass is O(n) time and O(n) space. Checking the map BEFORE inserting the current element is what handles duplicates like [3, 3] correctly and stops an element pairing with itself. Since the earlier index comes from the map, the pair comes out already ordered.
